Similar shapes have the same shape, but a different size. Every side gets multiplied by the same number. We call that number the scale factor, k.
Think about zooming a photo two times bigger. Each side doubles. But the picture now takes up four times the space.
Here's the whole lesson in one line. Lengths and perimeter multiply by k. Area multiplies by k squared. Volume multiplies by k cubed.
Sides first. A three, four, five triangle is scaled by two. Multiply every side by two, and you get six, eight, and ten.
Trap alert. Five, six, seven is wrong. That's adding two. Similar means multiply, never add.
Now area. A shape has area ten, and it's scaled by three. Area uses k squared, so multiply by nine. The new area is ninety.
If you said thirty, you used k instead of k squared. Area is two dimensions, so square the scale factor.
Volume. A box is scaled by two. Volume uses k cubed. Two cubed is eight, so the volume is eight times bigger.
Here's how to remember it. Length is one dimension, so k to the first. Area is two dimensions, so k squared. Volume is three dimensions, so k cubed.
Let's try an SAT style question. Two similar shapes have areas twenty five and nine. What is the ratio of their sides?
Areas use k squared, so go backward with a square root. The square root of twenty five is five. The square root of nine is three. The sides are in a five to three ratio.
Trap alert. Twenty five to nine is the area ratio, not the side ratio. Always take the square root to go from area back to sides.

The scale factor is six divided by two, which is three. Volume uses k cubed. Three cubed is twenty seven. If you said nine, that's area.
